image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a hammerhead shark swimming in dark blue water. The shark is viewed from below and the side, highlighting its white ventral surface and the underside of its distinctive cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head). One eye is clearly visible at the tip of the hammer. Other sharks are visible in the blurred background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is located precisely at the distal end of the lateral extension of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are on the ventral side of the cephalofoil and are not visible from this specific camera angle; they are occluded by the head's geometry relative to the viewer.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior (front) edge of the hammer is facing away from the camera or is obscured by the angle of incidence; only the ventral and posterior aspects are clearly defined.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image primarily shows the ventral side which is stark white/light grey, transitioning to darker tones on the upper edges, matching the counter-shading description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is on the top of the shark and is completely occluded from this ventral-side viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fin on the right side of the frame is visible, appearing broad and roughly triangular as it extends from the body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail (caudal fin) is outside the frame or heavily blurred in the background, making detailed structural verification impossible.
